country.note: A city state, so the capital is the country itself. The prime minister and cabinet answer to an elected parliament, the People's Action Party has governed since 1959 and Lawrence Wong has been prime minister since May 2024. Investors read this continuity as predictable policy, which Chapter 2 tests with the governance indicators.

country.name: Tuas and the reclaimed coast

country.note: An island on the Strait of Malacca that adds land by filling in the sea. The new coast at Tuas, Jurong Island and Marina Bay holds ports, refineries and offices, yet land stays the scarcest input, which is why land intensive production moves to the neighbours (Chapter 4).

country.note: Four official languages, Malay, English, Mandarin and Tamil, with English for business, connect Singapore to China, India and the Malay world. A third of the people are foreign workers, students and dependants, so the labour force can grow with demand.

country.note: The road and rail link across the Johor Strait to Malaysia, the federation Singapore left in 1965. Firms increasingly pair a Singapore headquarters with land and workers in Johor, the division of labour the Johor Singapore Special Economic Zone of January 2025 is designed to support.

sites.name: Pasir Panjang port
sites.note: Ships between the Indian Ocean and East Asia pass this port, so Singapore earns a living by moving goods made elsewhere. Feyrer's Suez Canal experiment shows that sea distance is a real trade cost, and the port exists to lower it.

sites.name: Jurong Island
rows: foreign value in refined fuel exports, 2022
of merchandise exports are oil made in Singapore, 2024
sites.note: Crude comes in and fuels and plastics go out. Refining is among Nunn's least contract intensive industries, and it lost its advantage as capacity grew in the Middle East and China, while Singapore's skill and contract intensive sectors kept theirs.

sites.name: Wafer fab parks
sites.note: Woodlands, Tampines and Pasir Ris host the wafer fabs. Chips are the infant industry that grew up without a tariff, drawn in by tax holidays in 1968 and moved up into fabrication from 1987.

sites.name: Tuas Biomedical Park
rows: RCA in finished medicines and biologics, 2024
sites.note: The second bet of the industrial policy, launched in 2000. Its plants built a real export advantage in biologics, while the industry's weight in value added and foreign capital at home shrank.

sites.section: Which sectors rely most on foreign inputs?
sites.name: one-north and Biopolis
rows: RCA in ICT and business services, 2024
sites.note: The research district. Fort shows that cheaper communication lets firms split production toward places with high human capital, so Singapore keeps the design and research stages while assembly moves to its neighbours.

sites.name: Central business district
rows: of the inward FDI stock is in holding companies, 2024
sites.note: Banks, regional headquarters and holding companies sit here, so much of the investment recorded in Singapore is money passing through on its way to the rest of Asia.

sites.section: What are its trade agreements for?
sites.name: Changi Airport and Airport Logistics Park
rows: of imports touched by non-tariff measures
sites.note: An air cargo free trade zone inside a country that already charges almost no tariffs. Because of that, partners rely on rules of origin to stop goods slipping through, which makes regional content rules matter for Singapore.
